items.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
items.job: Replace transmission with rebuilt or used unit
items.note: CarComplaints owners report about $2,100–$2,300 on average. A used unit costs less.

items.t: Rear axle cracking from rust (recall)
items.job: Free recall repair at a Ford dealer
items.note: Only free if the recall is still open on your VIN.

items.t: Front lower control arm and subframe rust (recall)
items.job: Free recall repair at a Ford dealer
items.note: Only free if the recall is still open on your VIN.

items.t: Head gasket leak and overheating
items.job: Replace head gaskets (both sides)
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $1,900–$2,600. Warped heads or engine damage add a lot more.

items.t: Intake manifold gasket leak
items.job: Replace upper and lower intake manifold gaskets
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $660–$890. Add an oil change and coolant flush if coolant got into the oil.

items.t: Cruise control switch can catch fire (recall)
items.job: Free recall repair at a Ford dealer
items.note: Only free if the recall is still open on your VIN.

items.t: Shudder or slipping from torque converter
items.job: Replace torque converter
items.note: CarComplaints owners report about $1,000 on average. Sometimes a fluid change is tried first.

items.t: Power sliding door stops working
items.job: Repair power sliding door motor, cable or latch
items.note: Owners report about $1,900 on average for the worst cases; a cleaned contact or a latch costs much less.

items.t: Interior lights flicker and battery drains
items.job: Electrical diagnosis and door contact/switch repair
items.note: One owner reports about $300 for a dealer to trace the fault.

items.t: Rear A/C blows hot air
items.job: Replace rear climate control switch
items.note: Typical reported cost is about $70. Blend door or vacuum repairs cost more.

items.t: Fuel line connection can leak (recall)
items.job: Free recall repair at a Ford dealer
items.note: Only free if the recall is still open on your VIN.

items.t: Check engine light from EGR pressure sensor
items.job: Replace EGR pressure (DPFE) sensor and its hoses
items.note: Based on YourMechanic estimates of about $163–$264 for this sensor on 1996–2003 Windstars (shop/dealer about $190–$430); no parts-retailer price was available, so the parts/labor split is approximate.

items.t: Rear brakes drag in wet or icy weather
items.job: Clean and adjust rear drum brakes; replace shoes and hardware if worn
items.note: Based on RepairPal rear brake shoe replacement estimates of about $250–$335 for 2000–2003 Windstars. A clean-and-adjust alone costs less.

items.t: Power steering fluid leak at the rack
items.job: Replace steering rack with a rebuilt unit and align
items.note: Based on estimator totals: YourMechanic about $970–$1,085 for the 3.8L (shop/dealer about $1,110–$1,710). CarComplaints owners report about $760–$1,130 typical.

items.t: Heater core leak
items.job: Replace heater core (dash work) and refill coolant
items.note: Based on RepairPal estimate of about $800–$840 total for a 1999 Windstar; no parts-retailer price was available, so the split is approximate. Owners describe it as an all-day job.
